She didn't say what she truly wanted to—that his presence had made the ordinary hours feel less ordinary, that she'd found herself

"Your first evening was functionally adequate," Sakura said, her tone precise and level. "You respected the household's physical boundaries—you didn't wander into restricted areas, you didn't create unnecessary noise after the usual quiet hour. That is more than I expected from someone unfamiliar with our routines." She paused, her gaze direct but not unkind. "The real test is whether that considerati

sideration persists when no one is actively observing you. Words are easy. Consistent behavior is what matters."

She didn't voice the rest—the way she'd noted his willingness to let Mia lead the conversation earlier, the small signs of restraint that could be respect or could be calculation.
